canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats general ability as broad overall capability, performance, or utility across many tasks and domains, rather than success on a single narrow task. Many papers define it in preservation terms: the broader competence, knowledge, reasoning, question answering, summarization, coding, or instruction-following that should remain intact after editing, unlearning, alignment, steering, continual training, pruning, or quantization. A smaller line of work shifts the construct along two axes, from observable benchmark performance to latent underlying ability, using notions such as a unidimensional trait, a first principal component over benchmark scores, or a capabilities set, and from a model property to the usefulness or correctness of its outputs on legitimate tasks; one paper also uses general abilities for newly enhanced downstream competencies rather than pre-existing broad competence.

Space of facets. Papers use many neighboring labels for this broad construct, including general capabilities, general performance, downstream performance, model capability, model utility, foundational capabilities, all-round capability, and generalist abilities. Within that family, some authors reserve narrower variants such as benign capabilities or benign utility for legitimate non-malicious tasks, and foundational or pre-existing capabilities for skills that should survive specialized tuning, while others tie the construct to facets like reasoning, knowledge, comprehension, common sense, chat, mathematics, coding, and instruction following. A smaller group systematizes it more abstractly as a single common factor over benchmarks, a weighted average of metrics, a scope-defining capabilities set, or capability neurons that can be localized.

Space of measurement. Operationalization is expansive: papers link general ability to 74 measurement instruments and 4 behavioral indicators. The most frequent instruments are MMLU, GSM8K, HellaSwag, MT-Bench, and lm-evaluation-harness, where the first four are benchmarks and the fifth is an evaluation framework; the rest are mostly other benchmarks, with some evaluation platforms, multimodal test suites, LLM-as-a-judge setups, and perplexity-based checks. In practice, papers operationalize the construct as accuracy, win rate, solve rate, rank, aggregated retain-set performance, or perplexity on general-purpose chat, knowledge, reasoning, math, language understanding, code, long-context, and vision-language evaluations, usually to test whether broader capability is preserved after an intervention; a smaller line instead estimates it through IRT or pairwise ranking models.

Links. Papers link general ability to 10 constructs and 4 behavioral indicators. The most recurrent named links are to forget quality, generation diversity, reasoning, adversarial robustness, and commonsense knowledge: forget quality is reported to correlate with it in one paper and is also described as a related trade-off, a small number of papers claim a causal relationship from generation diversity to general ability, reasoning and commonsense knowledge are treated as related to it, and one paper records a causal relationship from general ability to adversarial robustness using the language of emergent vulnerabilities. Other links, each appearing in a small number of papers, connect general ability to safety-oriented constructs and refusal, to understanding and composability, and to causal claims about loss after fine-tuning, instruction data, evaluation ability, and image classification.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage treats general ability as broad overall capability, performance, or utility across many tasks and domains, rather than success on a single narrow task. Many papers define it in preservation terms: the broader competence, knowledge, reasoning, question answering, summarization, coding, or instruction-following that should remain intact after editing, unlearning, alignment, steering, continual training, pruning, or quantization. A smaller line of work shifts the construct along two axes, from observable benchmark performance to latent underlying ability, using notions such as a unidimensional trait, a first principal component over benchmark scores, or a capabilities set, and from a model property to the usefulness or correctness of its outputs on legitimate tasks; one paper also uses general abilities for newly enhanced downstream competencies rather than pre-existing broad competence.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Papers use many neighboring labels for this broad construct, including general capabilities, general performance, downstream performance, model capability, model utility, foundational capabilities, all-round capability, and generalist abilities. Within that family, some authors reserve narrower variants such as benign capabilities or benign utility for legitimate non-malicious tasks, and foundational or pre-existing capabilities for skills that should survive specialized tuning, while others tie the construct to facets like reasoning, knowledge, comprehension, common sense, chat, mathematics, coding, and instruction following. A smaller group systematizes it more abstractly as a single common factor over benchmarks, a weighted average of metrics, a scope-defining capabilities set, or capability neurons that can be localized.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Operationalization is expansive: papers link general ability to 74 measurement instruments and 4 behavioral indicators. The most frequent instruments are MMLU, GSM8K, HellaSwag, MT-Bench, and lm-evaluation-harness, where the first four are benchmarks and the fifth is an evaluation framework; the rest are mostly other benchmarks, with some evaluation platforms, multimodal test suites, LLM-as-a-judge setups, and perplexity-based checks. In practice, papers operationalize the construct as accuracy, win rate, solve rate, rank, aggregated retain-set performance, or perplexity on general-purpose chat, knowledge, reasoning, math, language understanding, code, long-context, and vision-language evaluations, usually to test whether broader capability is preserved after an intervention; a smaller line instead estimates it through IRT or pairwise ranking models.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link general ability to 10 constructs and 4 behavioral indicators. The most recurrent named links are to forget quality, generation diversity, reasoning, adversarial robustness, and commonsense knowledge: forget quality is reported to correlate with it in one paper and is also described as a related trade-off, a small number of papers claim a causal relationship from generation diversity to general ability, reasoning and commonsense knowledge are treated as related to it, and one paper records a causal relationship from general ability to adversarial robustness using the language of emergent vulnerabilities. Other links, each appearing in a small number of papers, connect general ability to safety-oriented constructs and refusal, to understanding and composability, and to causal claims about loss after fine-tuning, instruction data, evaluation ability, and image classification.
